subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the approved surface be global, per-agent, hostname-scoped, or folded into broader egress policy?
rationale: The lower-level primitive exists, but exposing it changes a model-directed SSRF boundary and public config contract that automation cannot choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve a dangerous scoped policy
options.body: Land a narrowly documented SSRF policy design that allows private-network `web_fetch` only with explicit operator intent, cache separation, redirect checks, audit output, and metadata/link-local safeguards.

options.title: Keep only current narrow fake-IP support
options.body: Leave arbitrary private-network `web_fetch` unsupported for now and document trusted proxy or fake-IP options as the supported workaround.

options.title: Fold into broader egress policy
options.body: Route this through the broader web-tool egress firewall work so private-network access, domain allowlists, and per-agent authorization are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve a dangerous scoped policy
recommendation.body: Land a narrowly documented SSRF policy design that allows private-network `web_fetch` only with explicit operator intent, cache separation, redirect checks, audit output, and metadata/link-local safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent SSRF/web_fetch history and already framed this exact issue as a security-sensitive config decision.
